subject: Burst slotting and prompt/response length census for AtlasPilot pilot
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan@atlaspilot.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@atlaspilot.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing inputs: burst cadence, prompt lengths, concurrency targets

Hi Mateo —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving toward a short pilot and need a bit more granularity on the inputs you use for Dedicated sizing so our procurement team can sign off. Attached is a small export of recent traffic (workload-summary.csv). Can you confirm the specific numbers you need? Off the top of our head:

- Typical peak QPS we consider (for pilot): ~220 QPS for ~10 minutes/day during experiments
- Sustained QPS: ~8–12 QPS
- Average prompt length: 45 tokens (but we have long-form prompts up to 420 tokens in the training flows)
- Average response length: 120 tokens (some long responses to summaries up to 1,200 tokens)
- We stream ~15% of responses; the rest are non-streaming

Goal: get a preliminary estimate of required GPU slots and a conservative burst plan (we prefer to over-provision initial pilot).

Evan
CTO, AtlasPilot

Attachment: workload-summary.csv (CSV export, 42KB)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan@atlaspilot.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing inputs: burst cadence, prompt lengths, concurrency targets

Evan —

Thanks for the export — that helps. To produce a robust Dedicated footprint we try to get answers to a short set of focused items. I pasted a compact questionnaire below; if you can fill the bullets (or attach examples) we can run a conservative pilot estimate within 48 hours.

Quick questionnaire (short answers are fine):

1) Prompt distribution:
   - % of calls that are short prompts (<64 tokens): ___
   - % mid (64–256): ___
   - % long (>256): ___

2) Response distribution:
   - % short (<64): ___
   - % mid (64–256): ___
   - % long (>256): ___
   - % very long (>512): ___

3) Streaming: what percent of responses must be delivered via streaming vs non-streaming? ___

4) Session affinity & KV reuse:
   - Are you keeping sessions live with KV reuse? (yes/no) If yes, average tokens cached per session: ___
   - Average session duration (minutes) and session QPS per tenant (if multi-tenant): ___

5) Reranking / multi-step flows:
   - % of requests that perform a 2+ step flow (e.g., generate -> rerank -> refine): ___
   - Typical token amplification (total tokens consumed across steps vs single-step): ___

6) Peak shape and burst cadence:
   - For a typical peak minute, do you see a single tight spike (seconds) or a sustained elevated minute? Example: 220 QPS for 10 minutes as you noted vs 2,500 QPS for 30s.___

7) Latency SLO targets:
   - P50/P95 response latency target (ms) and whether it applies only to non-streaming completions: ___

8) Fault tolerance and fallback:
   - If Dedicated is saturated, are you OK with fallback to a smaller hosted model with slightly higher latency? (yes/no)___

If you prefer, attach a sample of 200 requests (sample_prompts.txt + api-usage-sample.json) rather than filling percentages.

I'll loop in Marissa and Karthik for GPU mix and billing implications once we have the distribution.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_pre-sales-form.pdf (fillable PDF, 18KB)

On Mon, Apr 5, 2027 at 11:05 AM Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com> wrote:
> Evan —
>
> Thanks for the export — that helps. To produce a robust Dedicated footprint we try to get answers to a short set of focused items. I pasted a compact questionnaire below; if you can fill the bullets (or attach examples) we can run a conservative pilot estimate within 48 hours.

Thanks — pasted answers inline below (quick pass; we'll attach a sample file after the day):

1) Prompt distribution:
   - % short (<64 tokens): 38%
   - % mid (64–256): 47%
   - % long (>256): 15%

2) Response distribution:
   - % short (<64): 22%
   - % mid (64–256): 55%
   - % long (>256): 20%
   - % very long (>512): 3%

3) Streaming: 18% of responses require streaming (mostly live summarization flows)

4) Session affinity & KV reuse:
   - Yes, we keep sessions live for agents. Average cached tokens: 640 tokens per session
   - Average session duration: 22 minutes; average session QPS per active tenant: 1.2

5) Reranking / multi-step flows:
   - ~9% of requests are multi-step (2+ model calls) for candidate generation + rerank
   - Token amplification: ~1.6x on average (generate + rerank costs)

6) Peak shape and burst cadence:
   - Our spikes are bursty: typical experimental spikes last 30–90 seconds and can reach 3–4x baseline; sustained peaks (10+ minutes) are rare and tied to scheduled experiments. The 220 QPS is an averaged per-minute spike during experiments; instantaneous within-minute peaks reach ~480 QPS.

7) Latency SLO targets:
   - P50: 60–80ms, P95: 220ms for non-streaming short/mid responses. For long responses SLO is looser.

8) Fault tolerance and fallback:
   - OK with fallback to a smaller hosted model if we receive a clear signal and gradual throttling; cannot silently drop requests.

Attaching a 200-request sample and an API usage sample for token shapes.

—Evan

Attachments: sample_prompts.txt (200 sample prompts, 12KB); api-usage-sample.json (usage patterns, 50KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan@atlaspilot.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing inputs: burst cadence, prompt lengths, concurrency targets

Evan / team —

Thanks for the quick answers — very helpful. A few notes from infra/pre-sales perspective and what we'll propose for an initial Dedicated pilot: 

- GPU mix: for this profile (moderate bursts + long responses + KV reuse) we typically propose an H100-heavy pool for the pilot (1:3 A100:H100 ratio) because of the long-response and session-affinity savings. If budget is constrained we can evaluate a quantized H100 or mixed set.
- Slotting / tiling: we see two viable slotting plans:
   1) Conservative: reserve capacity for 480 instantaneous peak QPS mapped to 6 H100s with conservative batching and pre-warming (higher cost but less risk).
   2) Cost-optimal: commit to sustained baseline on 2 H100s + 4 A100s with burst autoscale and cross-region fallback to Hosted for excess.
- KV cache: with 640 tokens cached/session, memory-optimized instances and longer-lived sessions reduce token compute by ~12–18% in our simulations.
- Streaming pressure: streaming 18% of traffic increases slot occupancy; ensure streaming pipelines are pinned to a subset of nodes to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Next steps proposed (MAP):
1) We will run a short simulation (2–4 hours) against your sample_prompts with the two slotting plans and provide a cost and latency table.
2) We propose a 2-week pilot: warm-up, 1-week instrumented run, and a follow-up sizing readout.
3) Schedule a 45min sizing review with infra owners and your engineering manager — suggested windows Wed/Thu this week.

I'll prepare the pilot-sizing workbook once we confirm which slotting plan you prefer. Looping Karthik for contract/commit guidance.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Architecture — Redwood Inference

(attachment: none)

Evan —

Great — thanks for the sample and the numbers. Attached is a short pilot sizing proposal and a mutual action plan (MAP.md) that covers instrumented metrics we'll collect (P50/P95 latency, tokens per call, cache hit ratio, effective GPU occupancy). High level summary:

- Recommended initial footprint (conservative plan): 6 x H100 slots (pilot pool) with headroom for 3x instantaneous spikes via autoscale + fallback path to Hosted for overflow.
- Cost estimate: conservative plan ~ $X/month (spread across committed and burst usage); cost-optimal plan reduces committed cost by ~28% but increases risk of transient throttles during tight spikes.
- Metrics to instrument: P50/P95 latency (per prompt length bin), tokens per session, multi-step amplification, streaming fraction per node.

Please confirm a 45-minute window for a sizing call — propose Thu, Apr 8, 10:00–10:45 PT. If that works we'll send a calendar invite and kick off the 48-hour simulation run on your sample set.

Thanks — looking forward to it.
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
